data: © NASA/JPL/U. of Arizona — northern polar plain; first to confirm subsurface water ice on Mars.

First spacecraft to physically touch Martian water ice. Phoenix's robotic arm scooped ice that sublimated in front of its cameras within hours — direct visual confirmation of the subsurface ice that Mars Odyssey's neutron spectrometer had inferred from orbit. Operated 157 sols before the northern winter froze its solar panels.
Validated water-ice-driven Mars exploration strategy; baselined polar-region surface operations.

Phoenix landed at 68.22°N on May 25, 2008 — the first NASA lander to touch down in the Martian high arctic. Within days it had scooped up the first sample of Martian water ice and watched it sublimate in the camera frame. The lander operated for 157 sols until the polar winter killed it; CO₂ frost formation buried the solar panels, ending the mission.

Water, perchlorates, and the first Martian weather
Detection of perchlorate salts in Martian soil — chemistry that would shape every subsequent Mars-habitability discussion.
